payload.name: CareClinic Health Tracker
payload.description: CareClinic is a free personal health journal for recording symptoms, medications, mood, sleep, routines, and appointments in one place. It helps people and caregivers keep an organized record over time and prepare shareable summaries for conversations with clinicians. It is a self-management and organization tool and does not diagnose conditions or replace professional care.

payload.name: Special Needs Jobs
payload.description:
Hi there,

I'm Kyle, and I run Special Needs Jobs over at specialneedsjobs.org. It's a free job board for ABA therapy roles across the US: BCBAs, RBTs, and behavior technicians, with pay, location, and work setting on each listing, plus free job alerts by email.

I was looking through your resources page and thought we could be a helpful addition for your readers. Would you consider adding us?

Thanks for the work you do,
Kyle

payload.name: MedicaidWorkCheck.com
payload.description: MedicaidWorkCheck.com is an independent, plain-English information site about the new federal Medicaid work requirement. Free tools include an 8-question exemption checker that becomes a private 80-hour monthly work tracker (no sign-up; all data stays in the visitor's browser), plain-English guides to every exemption category, 51 state-by-state guides, a living lawsuit tracker, and a full Spanish-language section.

payload.name: WatchToText
payload.description: WatchToText turns a public YouTube, TikTok or Instagram video link into a readable transcript. Paste the link, read the text in the browser, copy it, or download it as a TXT file. Useful for note-taking, captions review, and making video content accessible to people who prefer reading. Free to use, no sign-up.

payload.name: HealStroke: Stroke Recovery
payload.description:
HealStroke: Stroke Recovery is an iPhone, iPad and Android app from Stroke Technology, Inc. for adults organizing daily life after stroke and the family members or caregivers supporting them.

Publisher-described tools include a daily plan, guided speech and movement practice, medication reminders, progress and vital-sign logs, and plain-language educational resources. The app is a free download with in-app purchases; check the stores for current pricing. It provides education and self-management support alongside professional care and does not replace assessment, treatment or emergency care.

Please consider it for the Caregiver Apps directory, with its adult stroke-survivor focus clearly identified. This submission does not claim independently established clinical effectiveness or accessibility certification.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/healstroke-stroke-recovery/id6795639108
Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.stroketech.healstroke

payload.name: ToText
payload.description: ToText is an iPhone app by LovelaceLoom that turns spoken content, such as lectures, conversations, calls and voice notes, into written text with a summary and task list. People who prefer reading to listening, or who find typing hard, can review recordings as text, and the built-in dictation keyboard lets them write by voice in any app. Freemium.

payload.name: Special Needs Care Network
payload.description: Special Needs Care Network is a free matching service and directory that helps families find ABA therapy providers, special education schools, speech therapy and therapeutic programs in all 50 states. Families share what their child needs, their age and location, and get matched with specialized schools, ABA providers and therapy centers. Over 9,000 listings with real parent reviews; free for families.

payload.name: Special Needs Jobs
payload.description: Special Needs Jobs is a free U.S. job board for ABA therapy careers, listing current openings for BCBAs, RBTs, BCaBAs and behavior technicians from ABA providers. Jobs can be filtered by credential, employer, location, work arrangement, employment type and disclosed pay, and candidates apply directly on the employer site. It also publishes career resources such as an ABA salary guide and a job offer checklist. Not affiliated with the BACB.

payload.name: Local Senior Advisor
payload.description: Local Senior Advisor is a better way to find assisted living, memory care, and independent living. The online directory lists every community with the most current, accurate information. It also pairs you with a local senior advisor who has personally visited each community and can answer your questions about its services, costs, and availability. Local Senior Advisor is a free service to families.

payload.name: Autism Dating
payload.description: Autism Dating helps adults on the autism spectrum meet people who value clear talk and kind company, for companionship or something serious. ADHD and AuDHD members are welcome.

payload.name: Disabled Contacts
payload.description: Disabled Contacts is a UK dating site for disabled singles and the people who want to meet them, across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Members share what they choose about their disability, when they choose.

payload.name: AccessAble: free compression sock printable and Easier Mornings email
payload.description: Free one-page printable, "Putting compression socks on," with plain steps for one working hand or a helping hand: set up, position the foot section, make each pull smaller, smooth and check, plus a short box for caregivers. Also a free email, Easier Mornings, with one practical dressing and compression sock idea every other Tuesday. Free to print, share and read. No purchase needed. Printable (PDF): https://accessablecompression.com/resources/compression-socks/compression-socks.pdf

payload.name: LawAsked
payload.description: LawAsked answers real legal questions in plain language for 12 countries, and every answer cites and links the official statute sections it relies on. Topics include workplace rights, tenancy and consumer questions. Free; an information service, not a law firm.

payload.name: anysign
payload.description: anysign is a sign language learning app for American Sign Language (ASL), German Sign Language (DGS) and Ukrainian Sign Language (USL). Short video lessons are recorded by deaf and native signers, with quizzes and a searchable video dictionary, so parents, siblings, caregivers and teachers of deaf children can start communicating in sign language. All ages. Cost: Freemium — free video dictionary and first lessons; subscription for full library. Available online on iOS, Android and the web. anysign does not provide interpreting services.

payload.name: Adapted Accessibility
payload.description:
Adapted Accessibility offers innovative accessibility products designed to help individuals with disabilities interact with technology, entertainment, and compatible devices more independently.
Its primary product is the impact switch, a modular-mounted 3D- printed accessibility switch that provides an alternative way to control compatible devices. Adapted Accessibility primarily serves individuals with physical disabilities or limited mobility who may have difficulty using traditional buttons, keyboards, controllers, or other standard technology inputs. As a division of Lifetime Assistance, the organization also provides meaningful employment and supportive training opportunities for individuals with disabilities. Its products are built with input from people who have firsthand experience with accessibility needs, helping ensure that the products are practical and meaningful.
impact switches are intended to support:
- Individuals with Disabilities: People who need alternative ways to interact with technology and electronic devices.
- Students and Schools: Students who benefit from assistive technology and accessible learning tools.
- Therapists and Healthcare Professionals: Professionals who incorporate adaptive equipment into therapy and assistive technology programs.
- Caregivers and Families: Those looking for practical accessibility solutions to support independence at home.
- Organizations and Educational Programs: Schools, rehabilitation centers, and other organizations seeking inclusive technology solutions.

payload.name: Resource Donation Program - Oley Foundation
payload.description: The Oley Foundation is a non-profit home nutrition therapy community and advocacy group.  The Oley Foundation understands that within the nutrition support community, some people may need help with obtaining enteral nutrition (tube feeding) formula and/or supplies, while others may have extra items to give.
payload.address: Albany Medical Center, MC-28 43 New Scotland Ave.  Albany, NY 12208

payload.name: Without Limits Collective
payload.description:
From Surviving to Thriving: IEPs, 504s and Beyond.  At Without Limits Collective, our mission is to empower families by providing inclusive, trauma-informed, and individualized support that honors every child’s unique strengths. We exist to help parents feel seen, supported, and equipped—because when families thrive, children do too.
Our focus is tutoring, advocacy, and school management.

payload.name: Switch! It Up Switch Adaptive Toys and Adapted Play Products
payload.description:
Made for Real Kids.  Adapted with Purpose.

Born from our own family’s journey, Switch! It Up understands how important trust, safety, and meaningful play truly are.

Our toys are thoughtfully adapted by hand and carefully tested to ensure reliable, responsive play — supporting independence, confidence, and joy, because play should be accessible to everyone.
payload.address: 18132 Knobstone Way Westfield, IN 46074 United States

payload.name: GoBabyGo (University of Delaware)
payload.description: Modifies ride-on toy cars so young children with disabilities can move around on their own. Started at the University of Delaware, the program has trained volunteers in more than 40 communities and shares its car modification designs publicly. Many local universities and hospitals run their own GoBabyGo builds, so check for one near you.
payload.cost: Varies by local program; often free to families

payload.name: Adapt to Play
payload.description: Gives adaptive toys to children with disabilities at no cost. A physical, occupational or speech therapist must submit the request on the child's behalf, and switches are requested separately. Check their site for current eligibility and the areas they serve.

payload.name: Switched Adapted Toys
payload.description: A nonprofit that publishes free how-to guides for families and therapists who want to adapt toys themselves, and also sells toys that are already switch-adapted.
payload.cost: Guides free; adapted toys for sale

payload.name: Santa's Little Hackers
payload.description: A holiday toy drive whose volunteers make simple electronic changes to toys so children with disabilities can play with them, then give the toys away. Its website also keeps a list of toy-adapting organizations across the country, which is a good place to look for a group near you.

payload.name: USA Toy Library Association - Find a Toy Library
payload.description: A national directory of toy lending libraries. Listings show each library's address, who it serves (including children with special needs) and what it lends. Roughly a quarter of U.S. toy libraries offer adaptive toys, so this is a good way to find one near you before buying.
payload.cost: Directory free; some libraries charge a membership fee

payload.name: LEGO Braille Bricks - Play with Braille
payload.description: A LEGO set with bricks that carry braille letters and numbers, designed so blind, partially sighted and sighted children can learn braille through play together. Once available only to schools, it has been on sale to families at LEGO.com since 2023.
payload.cost: Paid; check current price at LEGO.com

payload.name: Rehabmart - Switch Adapted Toys
payload.description: An online retailer that sells switch-adapted toys from several makers in one place, including Enabling Devices, TFH and AbleNet.

payload.name: Nisonger Center Toy and Technology Library (Ohio State University)
payload.description: A free lending library at Ohio State's Nisonger Center with more than 1,500 adaptive toys, switches and low-tech communication devices that families can borrow for 30 days at a time. Many of its toys come from Ohio State engineering students' Toy Adaptation Program. Confirm current hours and how to borrow with the Nisonger Center.

payload.name: enTech Toy Library (Spalding University)
payload.description: enTech is one of Kentucky's five state assistive technology resource centers, run by Spalding University's school of occupational therapy. Its toy library lets eligible families borrow up to four adaptive toys, switches or learning toys for four weeks at a time. Confirm current loan terms with enTech.

payload.name: Toys with a Purpose (University of Kentucky)
payload.description: A free online lending library of adapted toys, devices and learning materials for families in Appalachian eastern Kentucky. Run by the University of Kentucky with the Kentucky Appalachian Rural Rehabilitation Network from its Hazard site, with local students and volunteers helping adapt the toys.

payload.name: Tech Tools Lending Libraries - United Cerebral Palsy of Nebraska
payload.area: Statewide (Omaha library at the Munroe-Meyer Institute)
payload.description: United Cerebral Palsy of Nebraska runs lending libraries across the state with modified toys, sensory aids and adaptive switches that people of all ages can borrow at no cost. The Omaha library is at UNMC's Munroe-Meyer Institute, 6902 Pine St. Call to check hours and how to borrow.

payload.name: PNW Adapted Toy Library (PROVAIL and University of Washington)
payload.description: A free lending library of adapted toys, switches and gaming equipment that families can borrow and try at home. Run by the nonprofit PROVAIL with the University of Washington's Taskar Center and the HuskyADAPT student group, it was the first U.S. adapted toy library registered with the American Toy Library Association. Enroll through the library's website.
